## Why This Is Asked
This question tests extending boolean logic to 3-valued temporally indexed constraints and practical propagation strategies.

## Key Concepts
- Kleene 3-valued logic with temporal indexing
- Implication as not(A) or B and time-sequenced constraints
- Dependency graph and fixed-point backtracking

## Code Example
```javascript
function tigaImp(A,B){ // A,B in {T,F,U}
  const not = x => x === 'T' ? 'F' : x === 'F' ? 'T' : 'U'
  const or = (x,y) => (x==='T' || y==='T')? 'T' : (x==='F' && y==='F')? 'F' : 'U'
  return or(not(A), B)
}
```

- Verifying that all constraints evaluate to not-F.

- Kleene three-valued semantics (T>U>F) with ¬, ∧, ∨, and X→Y as ¬X ∨ Y
- Constraint satisfaction with non-F guarantees

## Why This Is Asked
Tests applying 3-valued Kleene logic to practical constraint propagation in a realistic, beginner-friendly scenario.

## Key Concepts
- Kleene 3-valued semantics: ¬T=F, ¬F=T, ¬U=U; ∧/∨ use T>U>F; P→Q as (¬P) ∨ Q.
- Backtracking propagator: pick a U, propagate through implications, backtrack if a constraint forces F.

```javascript
function not(v){return v==='T'?'F':v==='F'?'T':'U';}

function and(a,b){const order={F:0,U:1,T:2}; return order[a] <= order[b] ? a : b;}
function implies(p,q){return or(not(p), q);} // Kleene-style
```
